description: Committee recommends new transit bylaw with fines, bans, fare enforcement.
Non-service animals must be in kennels; children under six supervised.
New bylaw would take effect September 1, 2026.

chips.text: Recommended
Mayor Block raised concerns about allowing pets on buses due to allergies and potential conflicts.
Bus Riders of Saskatoon delegation raised concerns about pet policy and child supervision age.
Council amended staff's proposed pet policy, reverting to kennels for non-service animals.
Unclear guidelines exist on what constitutes a service animal and provincial regulation.
Delegate warned sporadic enforcement could lead to charges of harassment and discrimination.
Delegate suggested public engagement with anti-poverty, immigrant, Indigenous
Administration committed to review pet policy if it becomes problematic after implementation.

description: Transit implements policing, new bylaw allows tickets for fare evasion.
Education campaign and smart card system aim to boost compliance.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
Councillor Ford questioned separating deliberate fare evasion from poverty-related non-payment.
High school students are identified as a group frequently evading transit fares.
The true extent of fare evasion beyond the reported 1.8% remains unquantified.
Homeless individuals often cannot afford fares; Saskatoon's low-income pass costs $66.
Administration promised a full update on the transit policing program in Q4 this year.

description: Saskatoon Transit redesigns bus network for 2026 launch.
Public engagement continues to refine network design preferences.
Redesign budget is $100,000 over three years.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer questioned survey wording on bus stop distance.
Bus riders will provide feedback on proposed routes.
Exact amount of $100,000 budget spent to date was not provided.
Bus Riders of Saskatoon advocated for improved, hands-on public engagement.
Redesign aims to shorten walk-in distance for people with mobility challenges.
Transit staff committed the $100,000 budget will cover all project phases.

description: Saskatoon Transit expanded service to Brighton, Rosewood, and Aspen Ridge.
Ridership decreased 6.7% in 2025, but peak routes remain full.
City plans $23.5 million for new buses and improved Access Transit.

chips.text: City Manager explained Saskatchewan's unique untethered provincial revenue sharing model.
International students may be affected by ridership changes due to enrollment shifts.
Is 1% provincial transit funding average across Canada?
Access Transit denial rate reduced from 9.9% to 9%.
Staff committed to providing updates on summer and fall route adjustments.
